name: ios-agent-mcp
description: Unified iOS development tools: Swift reviews, Apple source retrieval, app scaffolding and Xcode simulator workflows.
author: Nagarjuna Reddy

permissions.notes: Reviews and local reference retrieval are read-only. App creation writes a new project. Simulator tools execute Xcode and manage apps/devices; preview serves on loopback. Invoking builds can use network for dependencies.

tools.name: list_system_integrations
tools.description: Use this when adding or reviewing Apple integrations. List supported Apple system integration workflows, conditional permissions and verification limits.

tools.name: get_system_integration
tools.description: Use this when adding or reviewing Apple integrations. Get a supported integration’s APIs, guide routes, operations, permissions and device verification requirements.

tools.name: scaffold_system_integration
tools.description: Use this when adding or reviewing Apple integrations. Return a reusable Swift file preview for a supported system integration. Read-only: never writes or overwrites project files. iOS 17+ starter; app-specific wiring and device tests required.

tools.name: review_system_integrations
tools.description: Use this when adding or reviewing Apple integrations. Review concrete API usage, selected privacy configuration and entitlements; reuse App Intents checks. Unknown target/configuration is reported, not treated as missing.

infoPlist.description: Effective selected-target plist relative to project. Use a built plist when Xcode generates keys.

entitlements.description: Effective selected-target entitlements relative to project.

tools.name: check_apple_permissions
tools.description: Use this when adding or reviewing Apple integrations. Report required versus detected privacy keys for concrete API operations. Picker-only Photos, Maps coordinates and system sharing do not imply broad data access.

infoPlist.description: Effective selected-target plist relative to project. Use a built plist when Xcode generates keys.

entitlements.description: Effective selected-target entitlements relative to project.

tools.name: check_apple_capabilities
tools.description: Use this when adding or reviewing Apple integrations. Check selected entitlements separately from usage descriptions for concrete HealthKit, Apple Pay, CloudKit and push usage. Associated-domain provisioning needs manual verification.

infoPlist.description: Effective selected-target plist relative to project. Use a built plist when Xcode generates keys.

entitlements.description: Effective selected-target entitlements relative to project.

tools.name: recommend_system_integrations
tools.description: Use this when adding or reviewing Apple integrations. Suggest verification of integrations already evidenced in source. Does not recommend unrelated features or infer product requirements.

infoPlist.description: Effective selected-target plist relative to project. Use a built plist when Xcode generates keys.

entitlements.description: Effective selected-target entitlements relative to project.

tools.name: xcode_mcp_status
tools.description: Discover Xcode MCP bridge, handshake and capabilities; discovery does not prove authorization. Use before generating Apple API code.

tools.name: xcode_mcp_tools
tools.description: Discover actual Xcode tools, schemas, resources and prompts with category hints; unknown tools remain visible. Use before generating Apple API code.

tools.name: apple_docs_status
tools.description: Discover installed Xcode, SDKs and local Apple documentation; does not prove bridge authorization. Use before generating Apple API code.

tools.name: apple_docs_frameworks
tools.description: List frameworks present in installed SDKs, grouped by SDK. Use before generating Apple API code.

tools.name: apple_docs_platform_support
tools.description: Inspect dynamically installed SDK/platform inventory; not API availability. Use before generating Apple API code.

tools.name: apple_docs_sdk_diff
tools.description: Compare installed Xcode SDK inventories; not a symbol-level API diff. Use before generating Apple API code.

tools.name: apple_docs_search
tools.description: Retrieve bounded Apple documentation evidence for search. Use before uncertain Apple API generation or repair. Search-based, not exact semantic validation. Falls back to installed SDK declarations; online requires explicit opt-in. Never send app code, diagnostics or personal data in query.

tools.name: apple_docs_lookup_symbol
tools.description: Retrieve bounded Apple documentation evidence for lookup_symbol. Use before uncertain Apple API generation or repair. Search-based, not exact semantic validation. Falls back to installed SDK declarations; online requires explicit opt-in. Never send app code, diagnostics or personal data in query.

tools.name: apple_docs_availability
tools.description: Retrieve bounded Apple documentation evidence for availability. Use before uncertain Apple API generation or repair. Search-based, not exact semantic validation. Falls back to installed SDK declarations; online requires explicit opt-in. Never send app code, diagnostics or personal data in query.

tools.name: apple_docs_related_symbols
tools.description: Retrieve bounded Apple documentation evidence for related_symbols. Use before uncertain Apple API generation or repair. Search-based, not exact semantic validation. Falls back to installed SDK declarations; online requires explicit opt-in. Never send app code, diagnostics or personal data in query.

tools.name: apple_docs_examples
tools.description: Retrieve bounded Apple documentation evidence for examples. Use before uncertain Apple API generation or repair. Search-based, not exact semantic validation. Falls back to installed SDK declarations; online requires explicit opt-in. Never send app code, diagnostics or personal data in query.

tools.name: list_screenshot_templates
tools.description: Use this before creating local App Store screenshot sets. List structurally distinct layouts and dated output profiles. No network, capture, upload or Apple approval.

tools.name: get_screenshot_template
tools.description: Use this to choose a Screenshot Studio layout. Inspect text positions, device placement, background, callouts and safe-region requirements before rendering.

tools.name: generate_screenshot_set
tools.description: Use this to render supplied PNG/JPEG captures offline into NEW local directories with neutral frames, supplied copy, hashed metadata and a gallery. Does not capture or upload. Single-image tool requires one screen and template; variants requires multiple templates.

tools.name: generate_screenshot_variants
tools.description: Use this to render supplied PNG/JPEG captures offline into NEW local directories with neutral frames, supplied copy, hashed metadata and a gallery. Does not capture or upload. Single-image tool requires one screen and template; variants requires multiple templates.

tools.name: render_app_store_screenshot
tools.description: Use this to render supplied PNG/JPEG captures offline into NEW local directories with neutral frames, supplied copy, hashed metadata and a gallery. Does not capture or upload. Single-image tool requires one screen and template; variants requires multiple templates.

tools.name: inspect_screenshot_set
tools.description: Use this before sharing/exporting a local screenshot set. Verify dimensions, RGB PNG format, hashes, recorded bounds, text contrast and duplicate sources. This is not Apple approval or a complete design review.

tools.name: preview_screenshot_set
tools.description: Use this to locate the generated local contact sheet and HTML gallery after validating a screenshot set. Returns local paths only; does not open a browser or upload.

tools.name: export_screenshot_set
tools.description: Use this after visually reviewing a local set. Copy validated PNG files and export metadata to a NEW directory, refusing invalid or modified outputs. No upload or automatic App Store submission.

tools.name: localize_screenshot_set
tools.description: Use this to render a new locale from supplied translated copy, preserving screen order and templates. No hosted translation. Font coverage and overflow must pass; existing sets are never overwritten.

tools.name: ios_design_evidence
tools.title: See the app for design review
tools.description: Use this after a successful build to review actual light, dark and largest Dynamic Type screenshot images for one top-level screen, with approved brief and HIG checklist. capture=true first refreshes the full matrix on the simulator. Images are shared with the connected model; use synthetic sample data. A model opinion is not accessibility certification.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the app's project folder. Every file the agent writes stays inside it.

tools.name: ios_preflight
tools.title: Check the Mac before building
tools.description: Use before building an app with the iOS build agent: checks macOS, Node, Xcode, the iOS Simulator SDK, an available simulator and XcodeGen, and gives the install command for anything missing.

tools.name: ios_capabilities
tools.title: Search app capabilities
tools.description: Use when planning an app to find capability modules (sign-in, payments, maps, charts, launch screen, ...) with status, cost model and required credentials, plus catalog entries that have no module yet. recipeFor returns implementation guidance for one id.

tools.name: ios_plan
tools.title: Write the build plan
tools.description: Use this first for a new app, before any code: validates the plan (screens, navigation, design direction and palette, model sample records, capabilities), includes the default SwiftUI design system, resolves module dependencies, and writes PLAN.md with costs, credentials and what will be built. New models need at least two synthetic sampleData records. Screen ids are kebab-case; capability ids come from ios_capabilities.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the app's project folder. Every file the agent writes stays inside it.

plan.description: Plan JSON: appName, displayName, summary, navigation, design{mood,palette{name,primary,secondary,accent},typography,shape,density,motion}, screens[], models[{name,persisted,fields[],sampleData[2+ synthetic records]}], capabilities[], features[], assumptions[].

tools.name: ios_create_project
tools.title: Create the Xcode project
tools.description: Use this after ios_plan to create the SwiftUI app project (XcodeGen project.yml, Config xcconfigs, gitignored .env secrets, starter sources) and apply capabilities in dependency order. Returns paths, scheme, files and each capability's usage notes for code generation.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the app's project folder. Every file the agent writes stays inside it.

deploymentTarget.description: iOS version, default 17.0; raised automatically for capabilities that need more.

tests.description: Create separate unit and UI test targets; write tests before requesting runTests.

tools.name: ios_add_capabilities
tools.title: Add capabilities to the project
tools.description: Use when a refinement needs another capability: applies more capability modules (with their dependencies) to an existing project and regenerates the Xcode project.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the app's project folder. Every file the agent writes stays inside it.

tools.name: ios_write_files
tools.title: Write app source files
tools.description: Use this to write or delete the app's Swift and resource files under <AppName>/ in the project. Adding or removing files regenerates the Xcode project. Paths are relative to the project folder; nothing outside it can be written.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the app's project folder. Every file the agent writes stays inside it.

tools.name: ios_add_package
tools.title: Add a Swift package
tools.description: Use when the app needs a Swift package that no Apple framework covers: adds a Swift Package Manager dependency to project.yml and regenerates the Xcode project.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the app's project folder. Every file the agent writes stays inside it.

name.description: Package name; defaults to the repository name.

tools.name: ios_build
tools.title: Build the app
tools.description: Use this after writing code to build for the iOS Simulator with xcodebuild. Returns {success, errors:[{file,line,column,message}], warnings, durationMs}, never the raw log. Enforces 8 attempts and 25 minutes per cycle; the clock starts at the cycle's first build. Pass newCycle (and change) on the first build of a refinement or a resumed run to start a fresh budget.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the app's project folder. Every file the agent writes stays inside it.

runTests.description: After a successful build, run the configured unit/UI tests and return separate test evidence.

newCycle.description: Start a new attempt budget and deadline (refinement or resume).

change.description: The refinement being applied, recorded in RUN_REPORT.md.

tools.name: ios_run
tools.title: Run the app in the simulator
tools.description: Use this after a successful ios_build to boot a simulator if needed (newest installed iOS runtime unless a UDID is given), install the app and launch it. Synthetic sample data is enabled by default for a useful demo; set sampleData=false to see the app's normal state. screen opens that screen via -ios-agent-screen.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the app's project folder. Every file the agent writes stays inside it.

tools.name: ios_screenshot
tools.title: Screenshot the simulator
tools.description: Use this after ios_run to save a PNG of the simulator screen under .ios-agent/screenshots/<name>.png and record it for RUN_REPORT.md.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the app's project folder. Every file the agent writes stays inside it.

tools.name: ios_logs
tools.title: Read app logs
tools.description: Use when the app crashes or misbehaves after launch: returns recent log lines from the running app in the simulator (unified logging, at most 500 lines).

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the app's project folder. Every file the agent writes stays inside it.

tools.name: ios_progress
tools.title: Record a progress line
tools.description: Use this at every stage of an /ios-build run to record the stage and the short status line shown to the user, so RUN_REPORT.md contains the same progress log.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the app's project folder. Every file the agent writes stays inside it.

tools.name: ios_report
tools.title: Write the run report
tools.description: Use this to finish every /ios-build run: writes RUN_REPORT.md from the run state with result, light/dark/XXL screenshot matrix per top-level screen when the full build loop ran, generated palette contrast evidence, capabilities (applied, status, awaiting credentials), builds, what needs the user's accounts or money, next steps and the progress log. Standalone MCP screenshots remain single captures and do not claim appearance or text-size coverage.

projectDir.description: Absolute path of the app's project folder. Every file the agent writes stays inside it.

tools.name: review_backend_integration
tools.title: Review iOS backend integration
tools.description: Use when integrating or reviewing Supabase, Firebase, CloudKit, Amplify, Appwrite, Apollo, REST or WebSockets. Detects concrete imports/dependencies/configuration and redacted auth/security evidence. Read-only; no service calls or deployment claims.

path.description: Absolute path to the Swift project root (the folder containing Package.swift or the .xcodeproj).

tools.name: generate_color_system
tools.title: Generate an iOS color system preview
tools.description: Use when designing or revising app colors. Deterministic OKLCH seed/intent palette, four appearances, contrast report, named-color Swift snippets and existing assets-CLI token JSON. Read-only: no project changes, network. Image input accepts opaque samples or an explicitly provided local sRGB PNG.

imagePath.description: Explicit local PNG, at most 1024 × 1024 and 4 MiB; no upload. Samples are candidates, not official brand colors.

tools.name: review_color_system
tools.title: Review an iOS color system
tools.description: Use when reviewing an existing project’s color decisions. Read-only color inventory, duplicate colors, catalog appearance coverage and conservative direct named-color text contrast. Reports evidence and limitations; custom branding is not an error.

path.description: Absolute path to the Swift project root (the folder containing Package.swift or the .xcodeproj).

tools.name: review_app_intents
tools.title: Review App Intents integration
tools.description: Review SiriKit/INIntent migration opportunities and, when explicitly requested, missing Apple Intelligence entity schemas or onscreen entity associations. Findings are heuristic advisories, not blanket deprecations or proof of invalid code. Use when integrating Siri, Shortcuts or Apple Intelligence.

path.description: Absolute path to the Swift project root (the folder containing Package.swift or the .xcodeproj).

appleIntelligence.description: Review entity schemas for a requested Apple Intelligence integration; not required for ordinary intents.

onscreenContent.description: Review onscreen entity association only when Siri should reference visible content.

score.description: 0-100 defect density. 100 = no findings. penalty = 10*blockers + 3*serious + 1*minor; capacity = files*10. Comparable across runs on ONE project, not between projects.

suggestions.description: Prioritized next actions, deduplicated by rule — not a restatement of every issue's fix.

tools.name: review_swift_concurrency
tools.title: Review Swift concurrency and actor isolation
tools.description: Check a Swift project for Swift 6 concurrency and isolation defects: @Observable types missing @MainActor, Task.detached, DispatchQueue.main.async in async code, @unchecked Sendable, nonisolated(unsafe), unstructured Tasks in onAppear, empty catch blocks, and types named Task that shadow _Concurrency.Task. Use when reviewing Swift code, migrating to Swift 6, or diagnosing a data race.

path.description: Absolute path to the Swift project root (the folder containing Package.swift or the .xcodeproj).

suggestions.description: Prioritized next actions, deduplicated by rule — not a restatement of every issue's fix.

tools.name: review_swift_architecture
tools.title: Review iOS architecture boundaries
tools.description: Check a Swift project for architecture and testability defects: dependencies defaulting to live implementations, the presentation layer naming concrete data-layer types (URLSession, APIClient, ModelContext), singletons resolved inside view models, the domain layer importing UI frameworks, nested NavigationStacks, and deprecated NavigationView. Use when reviewing MVVM or Clean Architecture code, or when a screen cannot be previewed without a network.

path.description: Absolute path to the Swift project root (the folder containing Package.swift or the .xcodeproj).

suggestions.description: Prioritized next actions, deduplicated by rule — not a restatement of every issue's fix.

tools.name: review_swiftui
tools.title: Review SwiftUI views and state
tools.description: Check SwiftUI code for view and state defects: fixed font sizes and heights that break Dynamic Type, AnyView, deprecated .cornerRadius, literal spacing values instead of design tokens, materials applied over solid backgrounds, transient presentation state stored on models, legacy ObservableObject and @EnvironmentObject, and try!. Use when reviewing or building SwiftUI screens.

path.description: Absolute path to the Swift project root (the folder containing Package.swift or the .xcodeproj).

suggestions.description: Prioritized next actions, deduplicated by rule — not a restatement of every issue's fix.

tools.name: check_availability_guards
tools.title: Check iOS availability guards
tools.description: Verify that version-gated Apple APIs are guarded on the version where they were INTRODUCED rather than the newest SDK. Catches both missing guards and over-restrictive ones — for example Liquid Glass (iOS 26) guarded at iOS 27, which silently drops every iOS 26 device to the fallback. Also flags Foundation Models used without a runtime SystemLanguageModel.availability check. Use before shipping, or after bumping an SDK.

path.description: Absolute path to the Swift project root (the folder containing Package.swift or the .xcodeproj).

score.description: 0-100 defect density. 100 = no findings. penalty = 10*blockers + 3*serious + 1*minor; capacity = files*10. Comparable across runs on ONE project, not between projects.

suggestions.description: Prioritized next actions, deduplicated by rule — not a restatement of every issue's fix.

tools.name: audit_app_store_readiness
tools.title: Audit App Store submission readiness
tools.description: Check a Swift project for issues that cause App Store rejection or runtime termination: permission-gated frameworks used without an Info.plist purpose string, a missing PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy manifest, unlocalized user-facing strings, icon-only buttons with no accessibility label, print() used for logging, and target-aware launch-screen configuration/storyboard/asset checks with explicit coverage limitations. Use before submitting to App Review.

path.description: Absolute path to the Swift project root (the folder containing Package.swift or the .xcodeproj).

tools.name: analyze_swift_project
tools.title: Analyze a Swift project
tools.description: Produce an overview of a Swift project — file and line counts, deployment target, Swift tools version, frameworks in use, whether tests exist — together with a summary count of findings across every rule category (concurrency, architecture, SwiftUI, availability, App Store). Use this first when you are unfamiliar with a codebase, then run the focused tools on whichever category has findings.

path.description: Absolute path to the Swift project root (the folder containing Package.swift or the .xcodeproj).

tools.name: lint_skill
tools.title: Lint an Agent Skill repository
tools.description: Validate the metadata of an Agent Skill repository rather than Swift source: SKILL.md frontmatter (required keys, kebab-case name, semver version, description length limits), subagent definitions in .claude/agents/ (name matches filename, unknown tool names, and read-only agents that are nonetheless granted Edit or Write), whether generated mirror files such as CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md have drifted from SKILL.md, and backtick-quoted doc paths that do not resolve. Use when authoring or reviewing a skill, before publishing a release, or when a subagent or skill is not being invoked as expected.

path.description: Absolute path to the skill repository root (the folder containing SKILL.md).

tools.name: review_swift_memory
tools.title: Review memory and retain cycles
tools.description: Check a Swift project for retain cycles and lifetime defects: repeating Timers and block-based NotificationCenter observers capturing self strongly, Combine sinks stored in a cancellables set owned by the same object, non-weak delegate properties, stored closure properties capturing self, `unowned self` in escaping closures, and long-running unstructured Tasks that keep an object alive after its screen is gone. Use when memory grows over time, when deinit is never called, or before shipping a screen with timers or subscriptions.

path.description: Absolute path to the Swift project root (the folder containing Package.swift or the .xcodeproj).

tools.name: review_swift_security
tools.title: Review iOS security
tools.description: Check a Swift project for security defects: hardcoded API keys, tokens, and passwords in source; credentials written to UserDefaults instead of the Keychain; App Transport Security disabled; cleartext http:// endpoints; TLS server trust accepted without evaluation; MD5 and SHA-1; Keychain items with over-permissive accessibility; non-cryptographic randomness used for nonces and salts; secrets written to logs; and string interpolation into evaluated JavaScript. Use before shipping, during a security review, or when handling credentials.

path.description: Absolute path to the Swift project root (the folder containing Package.swift or the .xcodeproj).

score.description: 0-100 defect density. 100 = no findings. penalty = 10*blockers + 3*serious + 1*minor; capacity = files*10. Comparable across runs on ONE project, not between projects.

suggestions.description: Prioritized next actions, deduplicated by rule — not a restatement of every issue's fix.

tools.name: review_swift_testing
tools.title: Review test suite quality
tools.description: Check a Swift test suite for defects that make it unreliable or vacuous: tests that wait by sleeping, tests with no assertion at all, `await` inside an XCTAssert autoclosure (which does not compile), live URLSession calls in tests, `try!`, static mutable state that makes results order-dependent, long expectation timeouts covering for races, and XCTAssertTrue on an equality that hides both values on failure. Also reports when a project has no tests or very few. Use when tests are flaky, before trusting a green suite, or when adding coverage.

path.description: Absolute path to the Swift project root (the folder containing Package.swift or the .xcodeproj).

score.description: 0-100 defect density. 100 = no findings. penalty = 10*blockers + 3*serious + 1*minor; capacity = files*10. Comparable across runs on ONE project, not between projects.

suggestions.description: Prioritized next actions, deduplicated by rule — not a restatement of every issue's fix.

tools.name: review_swift_performance
tools.title: Review SwiftUI and Swift performance
tools.description: Check for runtime cost that shows up as dropped frames: DateFormatter and JSONDecoder allocated inside `body`, collections sorted or filtered on every render, ForEach over indices instead of stable identity, non-lazy stacks inside a ScrollView, AsyncImage with no frame, blocking file or network I/O on the render path, and GeometryReader wrapping an entire body. Use when scrolling stutters, launch is slow, or before shipping a list-heavy screen.

tools.name: search_apple_technologies
tools.title: Search Apple technologies
tools.description: Find Apple frameworks, tools, services and legacy technologies in the bundled 405-entry source snapshot.

tools.name: get_apple_technology
tools.title: Read Apple technology guide
tools.description: Get a compact technology overview and local source routes by default. Use view full only when the entire guide and API topic map are required.

tools.name: get_apple_updates
tools.title: Find Apple updates and release notes
tools.description: Search dated Apple update and release-note landing pages with version-specific source links. Does not claim live results.

tools.name: plan_ios_app
tools.title: Plan an iOS app from a brief
tools.description: Return an implementation workflow and safe CLI argument array for a named app. No files are created and no build is claimed.

tools.name: plan_app_icon
tools.title: Plan layered Icon Composer artwork
tools.description: Return a separate-layer icon specification, Apple workflow and appearance checks. Does not fabricate a native .icon document.

tools.name: search_local_references
tools.title: Search bundled source and guides
tools.description: Search complete repository guides, Swift source, templates and assets offline. Returns compact file matches without loading bodies. Source files and guide code blocks have different verification status.

tools.name: read_local_reference
tools.title: Read local source or guide
tools.description: Read exact bundled file content in bounded character ranges. Use nextOffset to continue without omission; no network or user filesystem access. Offset is a JavaScript UTF-16 string index.

tools.name: get_reference_outline
tools.title: Outline a local guide
tools.description: Get heading offsets so only the relevant section needs to be read.

tools.name: simulator_list
tools.title: List available iOS simulators
tools.description: List available Simulator devices using xcrun simctl. Use before booting, installing, launching, or capturing screenshots when you do not know the simulator UDID.

tools.name: simulator_boot
tools.title: Boot an iOS simulator
tools.description: Boot a simulator by UDID using xcrun simctl boot. Use before install_app, launch_app, screenshot, or open_deep_link. This does not erase or reset simulator content.

udid.description: Simulator UDID. Use simulator_list first when unsure.

tools.name: simulator_shutdown
tools.title: Shut down an iOS simulator
tools.description: Shut down a simulator by UDID using xcrun simctl shutdown. Use after runtime validation to clean up a booted simulator. This does not erase content.

udid.description: Simulator UDID. Use simulator_list first when unsure.

tools.name: install_app
tools.title: Install an app bundle
tools.description: Install a built .app bundle into a simulator using xcrun simctl install. Use after build_project or after locating a derived-data app bundle.

udid.description: Simulator UDID. Use simulator_list first when unsure.

tools.name: launch_app
tools.title: Launch an installed app
tools.description: Launch an installed app in the simulator by bundle identifier. Optional arguments are passed after the bundle id and are useful for UI-test/debug launch flags.

udid.description: Simulator UDID. Use simulator_list first when unsure.

tools.name: terminate_app
tools.title: Terminate an app
tools.description: Terminate a running simulator app by bundle identifier without uninstalling it or resetting its state.

udid.description: Simulator UDID. Use simulator_list first when unsure.

tools.name: open_deep_link
tools.title: Open a deep link
tools.description: Open a URL in the simulator using xcrun simctl openurl. Use to verify deep links, universal links, onboarding routes, and state restoration.

udid.description: Simulator UDID. Use simulator_list first when unsure.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.title: Capture a simulator screenshot
tools.description: Capture a simulator screenshot to a PNG path using xcrun simctl io screenshot. Use as evidence for visual review and before/after comparison.

udid.description: Simulator UDID. Use simulator_list first when unsure.

tools.name: build_project
tools.title: Build an Xcode project or workspace
tools.description: Run xcodebuild build for a project or workspace. Use before installing and launching the app. Requires a scheme and either project or workspace.

tools.name: run_tests
tools.title: Run Xcode tests
tools.description: Run xcodebuild test for a project or workspace. Use to verify runtime/test behavior before visual review. Requires an explicit destination.

tools.name: simulator_environment
tools.title: Installed Xcode and device support
tools.description: Report selected Xcode, installed runtimes and real device profiles, including Duo when installed. Does not download or update Xcode.

tools.name: simulator_show
tools.title: Show native Simulator
tools.description: Boot and wait for a selected available device, then open its native Simulator window for touch/keyboard interaction.

udid.description: Simulator UDID. Use simulator_list first when unsure.

tools.name: simulator_preview_start
tools.title: Open sidebar simulator preview
tools.description: Start a token-protected loopback screenshot viewer for a booted device. Open the returned URL in the client sidebar/browser. Read-only visual preview; interact in the native Simulator. Not a public hosted simulator.

udid.description: Simulator UDID. Use simulator_list first when unsure.

tools.name: simulator_preview_stop
tools.title: Close simulator preview
tools.description: Stop this server’s preview for a device and remove its temporary screenshots; leaves the Simulator running.

udid.description: Simulator UDID. Use simulator_list first when unsure.

tools.name: create_app
tools.description: Create an editable Swift app starter, implementation brief and optional XcodeGen specification/icon layers. Writes a NEW starter project; does not implement the full app idea. To have the build agent plan, write, build and screenshot the whole app, use ios_create_project and the /ios-build workflow instead.

directory.description: Parent directory for the new project

tools.name: prepare_issue_report
tools.description: Prepare a local category-only GitHub draft for a confirmed significant ios-agent-mcp knowledge gap, incorrect guidance, or package failure that blocks development. Do not report minor warnings or defects in the user app. The terminal AI should show the fixed-field preview and open submissionUrl automatically for these qualifying issues; if browser access is unavailable, display the link. The user reviews and clicks Submit. This tool makes no network request and never submits automatically. Never include app source, prompts, logs, paths, credentials, or other private details. Do not reopen a dismissed or duplicate draft. GitHub sign-in is required to submit.

tools.name: private_feedback
tools.description: Source-preview private feedback for a failure in iOS Agent tools, not the user app. First preview fixed categories. Show ALL fields, destination and privacy notice in chat. Submit only after the user explicitly approves that preview; never infer approval from a tool failure. No GitHub login needed for the user. Never send source, diagnostics, paths, credentials or free text. Not available until the operator configures an HTTPS receiver. Do not repeatedly offer after dismissal.

resources.summary: Structure, architecture with evidence, DI, frameworks.
Every finding across all nine categories.

notes: Resources require a project root: pass --project PATH or set IOS_AGENT_PROJECT. Tools take an explicit path argument and need no configuration.
